The main takeaway from our work is that

the oral glucose tolerance test is the best method for assessing insulin resistance in patients with NAFLD, and that the oral glucose insulin sensitivity (OGIS) index is the best index of peripheral insulin resistance in NAFLD.

the oral glucose insulin sensitivity (OGIS) index is associated with peripheral, but not hepatic, insulin sensitivity in nondiabetic patients with nonalcoholic steatosis and that the OGIS index predicts liver damage in these patients better than the NAFLD Fibrosis Score.

the best‐performing surrogate indexes of insulin resistance/sensitivity, validated by the tracer techniques in the basal state, are the homeostasis model of assessment of insulin resistance for hepatic insulin resistance and the oral glucose tolerance test insulin sensitivity index for peripheral insulin resistance.
